From c0e310188299358279fc27c88512f94db78991a6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Date: Thu, 27 Feb 2020 08:57:04 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] drm/i915: Skip barriers inside waits

Attaching to the i915_active barrier is a two stage process, and a flush
is only effective when the barrier is activation. Thus it is possible
for us to see a barrier, and attempt to flush, only for our flush to
have no effect. As such, before attempting to activate signaling on the
fence we need to double check it is a fence!

Fixes: d13a31770077 ("drm/i915: Flush idle barriers when waiting")
Closes: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/drm/intel/issues/1333
Signed-off-by: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Cc: Tvrtko Ursulin <tvrtko.ursulin@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Andi Shyti <andi.shyti@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20200227085723.1961649-1-chris@chris-wilson.co.uk

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c
index 0b12d5023800..7b3d6c12ad61 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c
@@ -453,6 +453,9 @@ static void enable_signaling(struct i915_active_fence *active)
 {
 	struct dma_fence *fence;
 
+	if (unlikely(is_barrier(active)))
+		return;
+
 	fence = i915_active_fence_get(active);
 	if (!fence)
 		return;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c`**
   - A new check was added at the beginning of the `enable_signaling` function to determine if the `active` fence is a barrier. If it is a barrier, the function returns early without proceeding further. This prevents unnecessary operations on barriers that do not require signaling.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a specific issue related to the handling of barriers in the i915 driver. The patch clarifies that before attempting to activate signaling on a fence, the code must confirm that it is indeed a fence and not a barrier. This change is a direct response to the problem identified in the previous commit (d13a31770077) that attempted to flush idle barriers when waiting, which could lead to ineffective flush operations. The patch aims to improve the robustness of the signaling mechanism by avoiding operations on barriers, thus fixing the bug reported in the linked issue.

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from the attempt to flush barriers during the activation signaling process, which can lead to ineffective flush operations if the active fence is actually a barrier. This situation occurs because the flush operation is only effective when the barrier is activated, and without proper checks, the code may mistakenly treat a barrier as a fence, resulting in unintended behavior.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void enable_signaling(struct i915_active_fence *active)
 {
 	struct dma_fence *fence;
 
+	if (unlikely(is_barrier(active)))
+		return;
+
 	fence = i915_active_fence_get(active);
 	if (!fence)
 		return;
 
 	dma_fence_enable_sw_signaling(fence);
 	dma_fence_put(fence);
 }

```c

dma_fence_enable_sw_signaling(fence);
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the code attempts to enable software signaling on a fence without verifying if the active fence is actually a barrier. If the active fence is a barrier, the flush operation will be ineffective, leading to unintended behavior during the activation signaling process.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (unlikely(is_barrier(active)))
    return;
```
Reason:
This check ensures that if the active fence is identified as a barrier, the function will return early, preventing any further attempts to enable signaling on it. This avoids the ineffective flush operation and ensures that only valid fences are processed, thus fixing the bug.
